result:
None of the three solutions reaches what I believe is the correct limit, 1/10. Solution 3 comes closest.

**The graph.** Write each vertex as a pair (i, j) with i < j. Moving one token by one step changes one coordinate by ±1, so the graph is the triangular half {1 ≤ i < j ≤ n} of the square grid. It has about n²/2 vertices.

**The limit.** The infinite square grid has domination density 1/5, so the triangle needs about (1/5)(n²/2) = n²/10 vertices. The boundary and diagonal only change this by O(n). The limit should therefore be 1/10.

**Solution 1** claims that one colour class of the bipartite graph is a minimum dominating set. That is far too large, since each vertex has degree at most 4. Its lower-bound argument is also flawed. Its answer of 1/4 is wrong.

**Solution 2** claims the graph is tripartite by difference mod 3, and that each vertex has degree 2. Both claims are false. The answer of 1/6 is wrong.

**Solution 3** correctly identifies the grid structure and derives the 1/10 estimate. It then replaces it with an unsupported 1/8, so its final answer is also wrong. It is still the closest.

CHOICE: 3
